answer_key.description: This dataset represents adversaries reading credentials from the memory contents of lsass.exe. One popular tool performing this behavior is Mimikatz.

verdict.assessment: User pgustavo executed an in-memory PowerShell-based mimikatz tool to extract credentials from lsass.exe and the SAM database, then established an outbound HTTPS connection to 51.143.111.7 for potential exfiltration.

findings.name: LSASS Memory
findings.behavior: PowerShell process accessed lsass.exe memory and SAM_SERVER/SAM_DOMAIN objects to extract credentials using in-memory mimikatz.
findings.reasoning: PowerShell accessed lsass.exe with memory read/write permissions (0x1438) and the mimikatz banner appears in PowerShell output, indicating in-memory credential extraction from LSASS. While SAM_SERVER/SAM_DOMAIN handles were also requested, the primary objective and evidence points to LSASS memory dumping rather than SAM registry access.

findings.name: Reflective Code Loading
findings.behavior: PowerShell loaded and executed binary payload in-memory using reflection (Compare-Object, Add-Member with PE header structures).
findings.reasoning: The evidence shows PowerShell using Compare-Object to process binary data and Add-Member to construct PE header structures (OriginalImageBase, SizeOfHeaders, DllCharacteristics) in memory, which is the hallmark of reflective code loading. This technique loads a binary payload directly into the current process's memory space without creating a new process or file on disk.
